- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). input.prompt:
Search this repository very thoroughly for a Markdown processing interface/abstraction. I need to find:
1. An interface (trait, abstract class, protocol, or TypeScript interface) related to markdown processing/rendering/parsing
2. Concrete implementations of that interface
3. Where those implementations are constructed/instantiated
4. Which components hold references to the interface type

Search broadly across the codebase - look for terms like "markdown", "Markdown", "MarkdownProcessor", "MarkdownRenderer", "MarkdownParser", etc. Check both TypeScript/JavaScript and any other languages present. Report file paths and line numbers for everything you find.

content.text:
Here is a comprehensive report of all findings.

---

## 1. The Primary Markdown Processing Interface (Go)

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 31-55

The `Service` interface is defined in the `markdown` package:

```go
type Service interface {
    ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
    ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
    ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
    RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)
    RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)
    GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)
    ValidateContent(content []byte) error
    RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
}
```

---

## 2. Concrete Implementation of the Interface

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 58-60

The sole concrete implementation is the unexported `service` struct:

```go
type service struct {
    md goldmark.Markdown
}
```

This struct implements every method of `Service` in the same file (lines 116-488): `ExtractTags` (line 143), `ExtractProperties` (line 193), `RenderMarkdown` (line 244), `RenderHTML` (line 255), `GenerateSnippet` (line 264), `ValidateContent` (line 349), `ExtractAll` (line 356), and `RenameTag` (line 425).

**Constructor:** `NewService` at line 85 returns a `Service` interface value backed by `&service{...}`. It accepts functional options (`WithTagExtension`, `WithMentionExtension`) that configure which goldmark extensions are loaded.

---

## 3. Where the Implementation Is Constructed/Instantiated

There are **four** instantiation sites, all calling `markdown.NewService(...)`:

| Location | File | Line(s) | Options Used |
|---|---|---|---|
| **APIV1Service constructor** | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` | 48-51 | `WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()` |
| **Test helper** | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go` | 44-47 | `WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()` |
| **RSS test** | `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss_test.go` | 54 | No options |
| **Fileserver test** | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` | 427 | `WithTagExtension()` |

---

## 4. Components That Hold References to the Interface Type (`markdown.Service`)

Three structs store the interface as a field:

### a) `APIV1Service`
- **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, line 35
- **Field:** `MarkdownService markdown.Service`
- **Usage sites:**
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108 -- calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447 -- same function for updates
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`, line 32 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll(...)` to resolve @mentions
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, line 85 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(...)` for webhook payloads
  - `/bench/repo/server/server.go`, line 85 -- passes `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` to `rss.NewRSSService()`

### b) `RSSService`
- **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`, line 45
- **Field:** `MarkdownService markdown.Service`
- **Constructor:** `NewRSSService(...)` at line 58 accepts the service via parameter
- **Usage:** line 339 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML(...)` to convert memo content to HTML for RSS feeds

### c) `memopayload.Runner`
- **File:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, line 16
- **Field:** `MarkdownService markdown.Service`
- **Constructor:** `NewRunner(...)` at line 19 accepts the service via parameter
- **Usage:** line 52 -- calls `RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService)`

### d) Function parameter (not a struct field)
- **File:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, line 74
- `RebuildMemoPayload(...)` accepts `markdownService markdown.Service` as a parameter and calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(...)` at line 80

---

## 5. Supporting Backend Types

The markdown package also contains these supporting files:

- **AST node types:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/ast/tag.go` and `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/ast/mention.go` -- custom goldmark AST nodes (`TagNode`, `MentionNode`)
- **Parser extensions:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/parser/tag.go` and `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/parser/mention.go` -- goldmark inline parsers
- **Goldmark extension wiring:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/tag.go` and `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/mention.go` -- register parsers/renderers with goldmark
- **Markdown-to-markdown renderer:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go` -- `MarkdownRenderer` struct (not an interface implementation itself; it is a concrete helper used by the `service.RenderMarkdown` and `service.RenameTag` methods)

---

## 6. Frontend TypeScript (No Service Interface, But Relevant Abstractions)

The frontend does **not** define a markdown processing service interface. Instead it uses the `react-markdown` library with plugin pipelines. However, these TypeScript interfaces exist:

- **`EditorController`** at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/types/editorController.ts`, line 8 -- an interface through which the editor exposes markdown get/set operations (`getMarkdown()`, `setMarkdown()`, `insertMarkdown()`). This is the closest frontend equivalent to a markdown processing abstraction.

- **`ReactMarkdownProps`** at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoContent/markdown/types.ts`, line 7 -- shared props interface for custom react-markdown component overrides.

- **`MarkdownRenderContextValue`** at `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoContent/MarkdownRenderContext.tsx`, line 3 -- React context carrying block-nesting depth during rendering.

- **AST node type interfaces** at `/bench/repo/web/src/types/markdown.ts` -- `TagNode` (line 4), `MentionNode` (line 9), plus type guard functions `isTagElement`, `isMentionElement`, `isTaskListItemElement`.

- **`MarkdownEdit`** at `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/markdown-task-actions.ts`, line 12 -- interface for describing edits to markdown source text.

---

## Summary

The central markdown processing abstraction is the **Go interface `markdown.Service`** defined at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`. It has a **single concrete implementation** (the unexported `service` struct at line 58 in the same file), constructed via `NewService()` at line 85. Three struct types hold references to this interface: `APIV1Service`, `RSSService`, and `memopayload.Runner`. The service is instantiated in production at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48` and then shared with the RSS service at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:85`.
